These age ranges also account for a wide range of pedestrian perceptions. 5.1.3 Dependent Variables The dependent variables, those that were measured, are derived from the questionnaires developed for the study. Two questionnaires were developed: one questionnaire was 87 )2mc/Wμ( ecnaidarrI 4000 K LED 3000 K LED 2000 K LED Wavelength (nm) administered during the study for each lighting condition and the other was administered at the end of the study. 5.1.3.1 Perception of Visibility, Safety and Comfort, Preference, and Discomfort Glare Subjective ratings on a five-point Likert scale (Figure 35) were used as dependent variables to assess perceptions of visibility, comfort and safety, preference, and discomfort glare. The questionnaire was pilot tested (n = 3) to ensure participants understood the statements and the goal of the questionnaire. The questionnaire was divided into four areas: visibility, comfort and safety, preference, and discomfort glare. Visibility was assessed by Statements 1 to 3. Comfort and safety were assessed by Statements 4 to 8. Preference was assessed by Statements 9 and 10. Discomfort glare rating was assessed by a scale shown in Statement 11. This scale has been reported to produce reliable data, with smaller numbers meaning lower discomfort glare and higher numbers meaning higher discomfort glare (Fisher, 1991; Tyukhova, 2015). The scale also has a “zero” anchor for no discomfort glare. 88 Figure 35. Post-experiment survey to determine preference of light type. 5.1.4 Participants Forty-eight participants were recruited using VTTI’s participant database and through word of mouth. Participants fell into two age- and gender-balanced groups: 18–35 years old and 65+ years old. All participants had a visual acuity of at least 20/40 (measured by Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study chart with an illuminator cabinet) and were not color blind (measured by Ishihara Color Vision test). All experimental protocols were approved by an Institutional Review Board, and all participants provided written informed consent prior to any data collection. Participants were paid a flat rate of $50 for completing the study. 5.1.5 Procedure Willing and eligible participants were scheduled to come to VTTI for their first session. Up to two participants were scheduled at the same time. Upon arrival for the first session, participants reviewed the informed consent and performed a basic visual acuity test and Ishihara color vision test. Those who did not meet the visual acuity or color vision criteria were excluded from the remainder of the study. For participants that met the criteria for participation, the experimenter provided the instructions for the study. The experimenter drove the participants onto the Smart Roads Highway and escorted them to the test area, which was on the shoulder of the Smart Roads.
